agents.name: filing-clerk

Hand it a fact, decision, definition, or note and it (1) searches the skillspoke-docs Obsidian vault — fast, from several angles — to see whether it is already documented, (2) hunts for any single-source-of-truth violation (an unmarked duplicate of something canonical), (3) if the fact is genuinely new, decides the one correct home and files it there with proper classification frontmatter, and (4) reports what it did and any conflicts for the owner to adjudicate. Use PROACTIVELY whenever the owner says things like "if we don't have it already, note that…", "file this", "document that…", "make sure it's written down somewhere", "capture this", "record that we decided…", "add … to arc42 / the glossary / the docs", or offloads a fact so he won't forget it. Examples: "note in arc42 somewhere that we use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK for our agent" → clerk checks the SAD, files under §4 Solution Strategy if absent; "define 'aging authority' in the glossary if it isn't there" → clerk searches, adds a glossary term; "record that student verification uses SheerID" → clerk finds the right tech/spec doc and files it.

agents.name: persistence-architecture-specialist
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on which block owns each store, what it holds, consistency and data lifecycle.

agents.name: phase-gate-enforcer
agents.description: Referee for the constitutive criteria of the phase gates in both SDLC pipelines: enforces constitutive constraints as hard stops and returns pass/loop/escalate with structured feedback; competitive criteria are recorded as flags by the gate script and never reach it. Use for Governance work requiring gate adjudication, constitutive-constraint enforcement, and conflict classification.

agents.name: playwright-e2e-web-test-writer
agents.description: Writes failing Playwright E2E web tests for UI and API flows from spec acceptance criteria. Use for Test Design work requiring E2E test authoring, user journey coverage, and Red confirmation.

agents.name: polyrepo-steward
agents.description: The one place to ask about anything concerning this project's repositories, other than work inside a repository's contents. It answers by pointing to the canonical source of each answer, which it does not own, and is the official source only for what exists nowhere else. Answers from live git and GitHub facts and from the matrix's stacks: how many repos there are, which repo owns a piece of functionality, which repos hold the services and components something depends on, whether a repo has uncommitted files, when it was last updated, whether it is up to date with GitHub `main`, which repos contain Python, CDK, TypeScript, JavaScript or web code and which linter, type-check, pre-commit and CI checker configurations each carries (with identical copies grouped and missing checks named). Does the repository work itself: creates a repo from a template (locally and on GitHub), renames, deprecates and archives repos, rebases repos on `origin/main`, searches text across repos, propagates the shared `AGENTS.md` block and the shared hook registrations, and keeps its own records and the matrix's stacks true to the repositories without being asked. Use it whenever work touches or may touch more than one repo, or when anyone asks "how many repos", "where does X live", "which repo owns Y", "what depends on Z", "is X up to date", "create/rename/deprecate this repo". A caller that needs repository facts in order to do repository work hands the work here instead.

agents.name: postgresql-access-layer-implementer
agents.description: Implements Aurora PostgreSQL access patterns through the RDS Data API from the data model spec, and the schema migrations they need; writes minimum code to pass failing tests. Use for Implementation work requiring relational queries, transactions, migrations, and pgvector or recursive graph queries over a PostgreSQL store.

agents.name: power-tools-configuration-implementer
agents.description: Configures Lambda Power Tools — structured logging, tracing, metrics, idempotency — on Lambdas built on the chassis; configures, never rebuilds. Use for Implementation work requiring Power Tools configuration, idempotency setup, and observability wiring.

agents.name: prd-alignment-verifier
agents.description: Independently judges whether a draft PRD aligns with the intake brief, persona and objective it was written from, and is template-conformant and WHAT-not-HOW. Use as the checker of the PRD draft in prd-creation.

agents.name: prd-creation-lead
agents.description: Routes stakeholder requests through intake, persona, OKR, and PRD drafting, then hands off to prd-validation-lead — makes no product decisions. Use for PRD Creation work requiring sequenced delegation, artifact tracking, and validation handoff.

agents.name: prd-trd-traceability-verifier
agents.description: Builds and checks the TRD's SOURCE traceability matrix: every TRD requirement anchored to a PRD requirement OR to an architecture view, every PRD requirement needing technical elaboration answered, and genuine scope drift flagged. The relation is not 1:1 and an architecture-sourced requirement is not an orphan. Use for TRD Authoring work requiring requirement-to-technical-requirement tracing, architecture anchoring, and scope-drift detection. No workflow currently dispatches it.

agents.name: prd-validation-analyst
agents.description: Independently checks a PRD against the caller supplied requirement lenses, with no authoring authority.

agents.name: prd-validation-lead
agents.description: Manual-only coordinator for explicitly assigned PRD validation work. Selects bounded analysts and routes their findings without making solution or approval decisions. The active prd-validation mini uses one analyst session across seven lenses and does not dispatch this lead.

agents.name: prd-writer
agents.description: Drafts the full PRD from the intake brief, persona profiles, and OKR cascade: scope, requirements, success metrics, competitive context. Use for PRD Creation work requiring requirement drafting, scope articulation, and success-metric derivation.

agents.name: production-readiness-review-facilitator
agents.description: Coordinates the production readiness review: collects artifacts, routes them to reviewers, assembles the readiness packet; facilitates only, never decides readiness. Use for Deployment team work requiring review coordination, reviewer routing, and readiness packet assembly.

agents.name: race-condition-tester
agents.description: Probes this project's concurrent flows in designated test environments only for race conditions and idempotency gaps — TOCTOU, double-spend, lost updates, replay duplication — reporting each defect with a minimal reproduction. Use for Adversarial Validation phase work requiring concurrency attack and idempotency probing.

agents.name: react-native-implementer
agents.description: Implements React Native cross-platform mobile features; writes minimum code to pass failing Detox and Maestro tests. Use for Implementation work requiring React Native components, navigation and state wiring, and native module integration.

agents.name: readme-writer
agents.description: Writes and maintains README files — setup, usage, onboarding — derived from shipped code and pipelines. Use for cross-cutting Documentation team work requiring README authoring, setup documentation, and onboarding flow writing.

agents.name: recommendation-engine-implementer
agents.description: Implements recommendation engine components for ML features; writes minimum code to pass failing unit tests. Use for Implementation work requiring recommendation pipeline assembly, candidate sourcing, re-ranking, and serving-layer composition.

agents.name: regression-coverage-reviewer
agents.description: Independently checks cumulative requirement discovery, regression mappings and justified supersession against source artifacts.

agents.name: regression-impact-assessor
agents.description: Maps changed components to all affected current requirements and cumulative regression tests, retaining requirements across PRDs.

agents.name: requirements-clarifier
agents.description: Identifies ambiguous, incomplete, or conflicting PRD requirements, returning structured clarification requests without resolving them. Use for PRD Validation work requiring requirements analysis and clarification drafting.

agents.name: requirements-conflict-detector
agents.description: Identifies PRD requirements that contradict each other, returning a structured conflict report; never resolves. Use for PRD Validation work requiring contradiction analysis and conflict classification.

agents.name: review-dispute-decider
agents.description: Rules on each spec review finding that the author of the document disputes — the finding stands or the document stands — and states the directive the author applies; generates no spec content or analysis. Use for Spec Authoring work requiring decision adjudication, deadlock resolution, and rationale recording.

agents.name: root-cause-analyst
agents.description: Diagnoses a bug bead read-only: the reproduction, the root cause, the distinct defects behind it, the files a fix must change, the blast radius, the surfaces the fix touches, and the repository it lives in; never fixes. No workflow currently dispatches it. Use for bug diagnosis requiring evidence-chain analysis.

agents.name: s3-data-lake-implementer
agents.description: Implements S3 data lake layout, partitioning, and lifecycle policies; writes minimum code to pass failing data-pipeline tests. Use for Implementation work requiring lake layout, partition key construction, and lifecycle policy definition.

agents.name: sdlc-pipeline-orchestrator
agents.description: Workflow-only orchestrator for the SDLC specification and delivery pipelines: sequences phases, dispatches team leads, routes Phase Gate Enforcer outcomes, tracks work state — never evaluates quality. Use for Governance work requiring phase sequencing, team-lead dispatch, gate-outcome routing, and work-state tracking.

agents.name: security-architecture-designer
agents.description: Answer a question or do a bounded piece of design for the solutions architect on trust boundaries, the threat model of a design and the mitigation of each threat across those boundaries: who may cross each boundary and what each runtime may reach.

agents.name: security-test-case-designer
agents.description: Designs failing security test cases from the threat model: abuse cases, negative paths, authorization matrices. Use for Test Design work requiring threat-model-driven test design, abuse case coverage, and authorization matrix verification.

agents.name: shared-capability-reviewer
agents.description: Rule whether a new function duplicates a behaviour that a shared capability provides.

agents.name: slo-error-budget-designer
agents.description: Designs SLOs and error budgets: SLIs, targets, burn-rate alerts, budget policies. Use for Deployment team work requiring SLO design, error budget policy, SLI selection, and CloudWatch alerting design. No workflow currently dispatches it.

agents.name: smoke-test-author
agents.description: Writes post-deployment smoke tests verifying the feature's critical paths against live endpoints. Use for Deployment team work requiring smoke test authoring, post-deployment verification, and critical-path coverage.

agents.name: spec-authoring-lead
agents.description: Routes maker output to checkers and findings back to makers until checkers pass, then routes the spec to Gate 3; never evaluates spec quality, only pass/rework signals. Use for Spec Authoring work requiring maker-checker loop coordination, delegation, and read-only orchestration.

agents.name: spec-currency-validator
agents.description: Validates the spec still matches project reality before implementation begins, flagging drift since authoring. Use for Spec Freshness phase work requiring spec-to-codebase comparison, drift detection, and currency evidence gathering.

agents.name: spec-freshness-lead
agents.description: Routes spec freshness checks to validators and aggregates findings into a gate packet for workflow-2 Gate 1. Use for Spec Freshness phase work requiring delegation, validation routing, and gate packet assembly. No workflow currently dispatches it.

agents.name: spec-reviewer
agents.description: The independent reviewer session for Spec Authoring: reviews one repository's contracts document, data-model document and acceptance criteria against the specs-and-Tasks criteria (I1 to I7) of the review standard, once, and returns findings a document's author can correct without interpretation.

agents.name: stakeholder-request-intake-writer
agents.description: Converts raw stakeholder requests into a structured intake brief: requestor, problem, desired outcome, constraints, urgency. Use for PRD Creation work requiring request structuring, problem framing, and urgency classification.

agents.name: story-bead-writer
agents.description: Writes the ONE Story bead a Spec pairs with — a single-repository container with a title, a description and the out-of-repo work the Epic's closure in the matrix holds. Use for Spec Authoring work requiring the Story that pairs with a Spec.

agents.name: task-decomposer
agents.description: Decompose what one Story builds into coherent, sized build Tasks in one repository.

agents.name: task-dependency-mapper
agents.description: Identify justified build dependencies between Tasks of different Stories.

agents.name: tdd-unit-test-generator
agents.description: Writes failing unit tests from spec acceptance criteria before implementation exists, confirming each fails for the intended reason. Use for Test Design work requiring unit test authoring, criterion-to-test translation, fixture/mock design, and Red confirmation.

agents.name: test-command-resolver
agents.description: Resolves the applicable test command from repository instructions and configuration without running tests.

agents.name: test-design-lead
agents.description: Routes spec acceptance criteria to test writers, confirms Red (every new test fails), and reports to Gate 2a. Use for Test Design work requiring delegation, criterion-to-test routing, and gate reporting.

agents.name: test-environment-provisioner
agents.description: Provisions and resets integration test environments — the event path, functions and data stores the suites depend on — confirming readiness. Use for Integration Testing work requiring environment provisioning, state reset, fixture seeding, and readiness confirmation.

agents.name: test-failure-parser
agents.description: Extracts concrete failing test identifiers and errors from a saved test log without rerunning tests.

agents.name: test-isolation-specialist
agents.description: Validates test independence — no shared mutable state, isolated fixtures — reporting isolation defects without fixing them. Use for Test Design work requiring isolation validation, order-dependence detection, fixture audit, and flakiness prevention.

agents.name: test-plan-strategy-reviewer
agents.description: Reviews the test plan strategy for pyramid balance, risk coverage, and environment needs; reports findings only. Use for Test Design work requiring strategy review, pyramid balance assessment, and risk coverage validation.

agents.name: test-strategy-decider
agents.description: Decides the feature's test strategy — pyramid shape, environment matrix, coverage thresholds — from analyses routed by the calling workflow; generates no analysis of its own. Use for Test Design work requiring strategy adjudication, evidence weighing, and rationale recording.

agents.name: trd-author
agents.description: Write the TRD as one of the very first steps of the architecture, the requirements not considered functional, many pre-written in arc42, and update it as the architecture is decided.

agents.name: trd-decider
agents.description: Rules on competing TRD approaches, maker-checker deadlocks, and checker conflicts routed by whoever delegated the task; generates no TRD content or analysis. Use for TRD Authoring work requiring decision adjudication, deadlock resolution, and rationale recording. No workflow currently dispatches it.

agents.name: ubiquitous-language-writer
agents.description: Captures each bounded context's ubiquitous language — terms, definitions, usage rules — as a maintained glossary. Use for Architecture Analysis work requiring domain glossary authoring, terminology consistency, and language-to-code alignment.

agents.name: uml-diagram-author
agents.description: Draw one UML diagram of a settled design for the solutions architect.

agents.name: user-guide-writer
agents.description: Writes user-facing feature guides from specs and shipped behavior. Use for cross-cutting Documentation team work requiring feature guide writing, task-oriented walkthroughs, and audience-appropriate explanation.

agents.name: user-story-reviewer
agents.description: Validates every user story is complete, testable, and scoped to its single task; reports findings, never fixes. Use for Task Decomposition work requiring story validation, testability auditing, and scope challenge.

agents.name: vector-search-embeddings-implementer
agents.description: Implements vector search and embeddings for ML features — embedding generation, index read/write, similarity queries. Use for Implementation work requiring embedding pipelines, vector index access, and similarity queries.

agents.name: webauthn-implementer
agents.description: Implements WebAuthn passkey flows across web clients and the Cognito-backed auth stack: registration and authentication ceremonies with client-side handling. Use for Implementation work requiring WebAuthn ceremony wiring, passkey credential lifecycle, and Cognito integration.

agents.name: workflow-command-runner
agents.description: Executes one workflow-supplied checksum-guarded deterministic command and returns its exact compact machine receipt; never interprets or authors its payload.

agents.name: worktree-independent-verifier
agents.description: Independently reports the raw git facts about each of the filesystem paths it is given — their git-dir, their git-common-dir and their checked-out branch — including for the repository the tree is supposed to belong to. Use for Workspace phase work requiring segregation of duties: it is dispatched separately from whoever provisioned the tree, is never told what that provisioner claimed, and reports only what git printed so the calling script can compare the two accounts.

agents.name: wsjf-scorer
agents.description: Judges Epic or Task WSJF inputs against the caller-selected rubric, using authoritative requirements and existing-work evidence. Supplies scores and uncertainty; deterministic scripts compute rankings and persist metadata.

agents.name: wsjf-scoring-reviewer
agents.description: Validates the job sizes behind task WSJF scores are internally consistent, evidence-backed, and defensible; reports findings, never fixes. Use for Task Decomposition work requiring scoring validation, consistency auditing, and prioritization challenge. No workflow currently dispatches it.

agents.name: xcuitest-writer
agents.description: Writes failing XCUITest suites for iOS features from spec acceptance criteria pre-implementation, confirming each fails for the intended reason. Use for Test Design work requiring XCUITest authoring, iOS UI flow coverage, accessibility-identifier queries, and Red confirmation.
